title: Explosive Training and Heavy Weight Training are Effective for Improving Running Economy in Endurance Athletes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Denadai BS, de Aguiar RA, de Lima LC, Greco CC, Caputo F
population: Endurance running athletes; 20 effects from 16 studies published up to August 2015
findings: Concurrent strength and endurance training had a small beneficial effect on running economy (% change -3.93 +/- 1.19%, p < 0.001).

Explosive (-4.83 +/- 1.53%, p < 0.001) and heavy weight (-3.65 +/- 2.74%, p = 0.009) programs produced similar improvements; isometric training (-2.20 +/- 4.37%, p = 0.324) did not produce a significant effect.
Meta-regression: the magnitude of running economy change was larger for longer training duration (beta -0.83 +/- 0.72, p = 0.02).
Authors conclude that explosive and heavy training are effective within a few weeks, but long-term programs seem necessary for the largest improvement.
limitations: Pre-2016 literature; small number of effects; meta-regression with many covariates on 20 effects is exploratory; sample size not stated in abstract; running economy outcome only. Crossref issued year 2016 (online first); issue year 2017.
implications: Use roughly 3-4% as the central conservative planning figure for relative oxygen-cost improvement from a strength block, with ranges of about 2-8% in individual studies.
Treat explosive and heavy work as comparably effective for economy in this analysis, and favor longer blocks over short ones.
